clue.text: A flower might sway the girl

parts.note: to rock is to sway to and fro
Rose is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A bloom nodding in the breeze might set a young woman swaying.
explanation.definitionFit: The rock rose is a low shrub of the cistus family grown for its showy blooms.

clue.text: Beer-maker caught King's Scholar in simple fiddles

indicators.note: a maker of the word beer reworks its letters into a new arrangement

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
KS stands for King's Scholar, at Eton

explanation.surface: A brewer catches a scholar playing rustic violins.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebeck is a medieval bowed string instrument, a primitive violin.

clue.text: Contributing four-point conclusion to study of the French Communist leader

indicators.note: the four-point piece comes as the conclusion, placed after everything else

parts.note: to con is to study
du is French for of the

indicators.note: the leader of the word Communist is its first letter

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals and E is a compass point

explanation.surface: A four-point summary added to a study of a French party leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Something helping to bring about an outcome is said to be favourable to it.

clue.text: A favour to trees, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A good turn done for some trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A favour is a ribbon badge or rosette worn as a token.

clue.text: How swift Camilla cleaned up the plain ? (Pope)

definitions.text: How swift Camilla cleaned up the plain ? (Pope)

parts.words: How swift Camilla cleaned up the plain ? (Pope)
parts.note: Pope's Essay on Criticism says swift Camilla moved rapidly over the plain, using a verb that also means cleaned by rubbing

explanation.surface: A literary question about Pope's fleet Camilla and the plain.
explanation.walkthrough: Alexander Pope wrote of the warrior maiden that 'swift Camilla' passes over the plain; the verb also means scrubbed clean.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both ranged swiftly over and scrubbed hard to clean.

clue.text: Airborne type is piano devotee

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
a devotee of something is a lover of it

explanation.surface: Someone who flies around turns out to be a keen fan of the piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A wading bird of the shore and moor, so a flying sort of creature.

clue.text: Fruit of trench warfare

definitions.meaning: a tropical fruit with spiky skin
slang for a hand grenade, from its segmented shape

explanation.surface: What trench fighting produced.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropical fruit lent its name to the ridged hand grenade of the First World War.

clue.text: Result of unfashionable act

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
a turn is an act in a variety show

explanation.surface: The consequence of some old-fashioned stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: The quantity produced or the outcome of a process.

clue.text: Meet Rex by arrangement in the end

indicators.note: by arrangement says the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Meeting Rex was finally arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The utmost point or furthest limit of something.

clue.text: Female slaves of Fleming's fiction ?

parts.note: Ian Fleming's fiction features James Bond, whose many women can be read as belonging to the secret agent; the phrase also means women held in bondage

explanation.surface: A question about the subservient women in Ian Fleming's spy novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Women held in bondage or serfdom are female slaves; split apart the term reads as the spy's women.

clue.text: Thank-you note for Harry

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
te is the seventh note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A short message of gratitude written to someone called Harry.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for 'thank you'. 'for' just links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Tate was a famous English music-hall comedian, so the forename points to his surname.

clue.text: Part of Shop Act with neutralizing effect

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for a noun: a step taken to neutralize something

parts.note: the counter is the serving surface in a shop
a measure is a legislative act

explanation.surface: A clause in some retail legislation that cancels something out.
explanation.definitionFit: A step taken to offset or neutralize a threat or another action.

clue.text: Send round cash gift as pay for the priest

indicators.note: the word send is placed round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a tip is a small gift of cash

explanation.surface: Instructions to post money as a present to pay a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman's fixed salary or allowance is the classic use of this word.

clue.text: Bowdlerize Miss Doolittle ? Out of the question!

indicators.note: to bowdlerize is to censor by cutting rude words, so the swear word goes

parts.note: Eliza Doolittle in Shaw's Pygmalion shocked audiences with 'Not bloody likely'

explanation.surface: A censor cleaning up Eliza's language, followed by an emphatic refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: Shaw's Eliza Doolittle famously says 'Not bloody likely'; Bowdlerize removes the expletive.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic refusal meaning there's no chance at all.

clue.text: Sir Patrick about to turn poet

parts.note: Sir Patrick Spens is the hero of a famous Scottish ballad

indicators.note: to turn tells us the short word for about is read backwards

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for about, concerning

explanation.surface: A knight named Patrick is on the point of becoming a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' reverses RE (about) to give ER, which follows SPENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan author of The Faerie Queene.

clue.text: Feeling Vi is tense and upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Vi is anxious and distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling as an adjective describes someone easily touched, responsive.

clue.text: Create an effect in the theatre

definitions.meaning: to work, take effect, as a remedy does
what a surgeon does in an operating theatre

explanation.surface: Making an impression on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug or force works when it has an effect; a surgeon works on patients in the operating theatre.

clue.text: Biased towards desirable match with Alfred

parts.note: a parti is an eligible person to marry
Al is short for Alfred

explanation.surface: Favouring a good marriage prospect, Alfred.
explanation.definitionFit: If you are fond of something you are inclined in its favour.

clue.text: Disparage detailed analysis

explanation.surface: Criticise a full breakdown.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb phrase it means to belittle; as a noun a full itemised summary.

clue.text: Inspired public protest by Northern Ireland Conservative

parts.note: a demo is a public demonstration or protest march

explanation.surface: A rousing street demonstration staged by a Tory from Ulster.
explanation.definitionFit: Possessed by a daemon or genius, as in frenzied inspiration.

clue.text: Like Africa before the dawn ?

parts.note: Victorian explorers spoke of the continent as unknown and gloomy, and the proverb says the night is gloomiest just before daybreak

explanation.surface: Africa just before sunrise.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of lightless, used both of unexplored Africa and of the hour before daybreak.

clue.text: Preparing the bases of Clerihew geography

definitions.text: Preparing the bases of Clerihew geography

parts.words: Preparing the bases of Clerihew geography
parts.note: E. C. Bentley's clerihew says geography is about maps, so preparing those is its base

explanation.surface: Laying the groundwork for a comic verse about geography.
explanation.definitionFit: Producing charts of land is the foundation of geography in Bentley's verse.

clue.text: Amusement halls are an offence in the island

indicators.note: in places the offence inside the island's name

parts.note: Cos (Kos) is a Greek island
a sin is an offence

explanation.surface: Gaming houses are wrongdoing on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Gambling houses are buildings for entertainment.

clue.text: Stitches during a race? Instant remedies, rather

definitions.meaning: stitches read as sewn mends done while running, rather than side pains
quick fixes made without stopping work

explanation.surface: A runner's side pains described, then quick fixes.
explanation.definitionFit: Repairs carried out while a machine keeps operating are quick on-the-spot fixes; read literally they are mending done mid-race.

clue.text: African Queen avoided action

parts.note: to avoid action is to have done nothing: did plus O for nothing
to avoid action is to have done nothing: did plus O for nothing

explanation.surface: A monarch from Africa who stayed out of the fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'avoided action' as 'did nothing': DID, then O for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dido was the legendary founder and ruler of Carthage in North Africa.

clue.text: Speed trip ?

definitions.meaning: promptness, haste in getting things done
a journey made for a purpose

explanation.surface: A quick journey.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both promptness (dispatch) and a journey undertaken with a purpose, such as an exploring party.

clue.text: Copious, if "corny ", , outpouring

definitions.meaning: the flood from the horn of abundance, which 'corny' hints at

explanation.surface: A gushing flood described as abundant, if a bit trite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corny' hints at the cornucopia or horn of abundance, whose outpouring is the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An abundance or profusion of things, as from the horn of abundance.

clue.text: Shocks bad for horses

definitions.meaning: a disease of horses and cattle causing a reeling gait

explanation.surface: Things that upset horses.
explanation.definitionFit: To astound is to make someone reel; the same plural word names a livestock illness marked by unsteady walking.
